title: About
text:
A little about me


Building the skills to make data make sense.



I’m a Computer Science student at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, interested in the space where data science, AI, and communication meet.


I enjoy organizing information, exploring patterns, and turning findings into something clear and useful. I’m continuing to grow my technical toolkit while building a thoughtful, practical approach to analytical work.







Outside the classroom


Gamma Phi Beta


My time in Gamma Phi Beta is an important part of my college experience. I’m looking forward to sharing memories from our Girls on the Run philanthropy and Big/Little traditions.

Areas of focus


Three parts of the process.





01


Data foundations


Organizing data and developing repeatable workflows for analysis and reporting.




02


Analytical methods


Applying predictive modeling, forecasting, and statistical analysis to practical questions.




03


Clear communication


Presenting technical results through visualizations and concise explanations.







My approach


Thoughtful at every step.




Start with the question

Understand what the analysis should help someone learn or decide.



Keep the process clear

Make data preparation and analytical steps organized and repeatable.



Explain the result

Share limitations and findings in language that makes sense to the audience.

title: Curious about data.Focused on what it can do.
text:
Keira Rish · Computer Science student


Curious about data.Focused on what it can do.


I’m studying Computer Science at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, with a focus on data science, AI, and analytics. I connect data workflows, analysis, and clear communication to make information more useful.


Explore my work A little about me ↗





University of Nebraska–Lincoln · Computer Science







How I think about data


From raw informationto useful outcomes.


Good analysis is more than a model or a chart. It starts with the right question and ends with a result people can understand.





01



Find the signal


Use analysis and visualization to uncover patterns and explain what they mean.





02



Explore what’s next


Apply predictive methods—from regression and classification to clustering and forecasting—to practical questions.





03



Make the work repeatable


Build organized data and reporting workflows that are easier to understand and maintain.








Current toolkit


Tools & topics


My focus is evaluating AI chatbots with LLM-as-a-Judge methods—analyzing outputs and measuring opportunities to improve.
